result:
The port is complete and the full suite is green: **773/773 tests passing across 6 files**.

## What's in `ported_implementation/`

`src/` mirrors the Python package module-for-module (kebab-case filenames, TS idiom):

| Python | TypeScript |
|---|---|
| `gbnf/GBNF.py`, `__init__.py` | `src/GBNF.ts`, `src/index.ts` (default + named exports) |
| `rules_builder/` | `src/rules-builder/` (`RulesBuilder`, `SymbolIds`, `parseChar/Name/Space`, `isWordChar`) |
| `grammar_parser/build_rule_stack.py` | `src/grammar-parser/build-rule-stack.ts` |
| `grammar_graph/` | `src/grammar-graph/` (`Graph`, `GraphNode`, `GraphPointer`, `Pointers`, `ParseState`, `RuleRef`, type guards, print) |
| `utils/` + `utils/errors/` | `src/utils/` + `src/utils/errors/` |

Python idioms mapped: dataclasses → classes with own `type`/`value` fields (so `toEqual` against plain objects works), generators → generator functions, `OrderedDict` → `Map`, `__iter__` → `Symbol.iterator`, exception classes → `Error` subclasses with identical message construction (`InputParseError.errorForMostRecentInput` is a getter, as the tests use).

Tests were copied in per `tests/javascript/README.md` and run with the globally installed vitest 2.1.3 (`npx vitest run --config vitest.config.unit.ts`, also `npm test`). No network, so nothing was installed; `tsconfig.json` is included but `tsc` isn't available in this environment, so the port is verified by the suite and by esbuild transform, not by a typecheck run.

## Two deliberate divergences from the reference

Beyond the test suite, I diffed the port against the Python on ~30 extra grammars/inputs (escapes, comments, `\r\n`, nested groups, all error paths). Everything matched except:

1. **Rule ordering.** `Graph` stores a `RuleRef`'s target nodes in a Python `set`, so the reference emits rules in hash order. E.g. for `root ::= ( [^abcdefgh] | [b-z])*` the Python yields `[end, char, char_exclude]`, while `iteration-with-an-initial-string.test.ts` expects `[char_exclude, char, end]`. I used an insertion-ordered `Set`, which preserves path order and matches the tests.
2. **Missing `root` symbol.** `GBNF.py` does `if symbol_ids["root"] is None`, which raises a bare `KeyError('root')` for a grammar like `foo ::= "a"`. The port throws the clearly-intended `GrammarParseError(grammar, 0, "Grammar does not contain a 'root' symbol")`. No test covers this case.

One incidental fix falls out of the port: `Graph.print()` reads `rule.type`, which doesn't exist on Python's `Rule` base class (it crashes on any path ending in `RuleEnd`); since the TS rules carry `type` as a real field, printing works.
